ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a horizontal thin film labeled with index nf. A light ray labeled “Light” is incident normally downward onto the top surface. The region above the film is labeled n1 < nf, and the region below the film is labeled n2 < nf. Reasoning: For reflected-light interference, compare the ray reflected at the upper surface with the ray that enters the film, reflects from the lower surface, and returns upward. At the upper surface, light reflects from a lower-index medium into a higher-index film, so that reflected ray gains a π phase shift. At the lower surface, light inside the higher-index film reflects from a boundary to a lower-index medium, so it gains no π phase shift. The second reflected ray travels an extra round-trip distance 2t inside the film, giving propagation phase 2π(2t/λ) = 4πt/λ, where λ is the wavelength in the film. Because there is one extra π phase reversal between the two reflected rays, constructive interference requires 4πt/λ − π = 2πm. Thus t = (2m + 1)λ/4, and the smallest nonzero thickness is λ/4.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: a normally incident light ray strikes a horizontal thin film of index n_f, with the medium above labeled n_1 < n_f and the medium below labeled n_2 < n_f. Use the text statement that the wavelength lambda is the wavelength inside the film. Compare the two reflected rays: one reflected at the upper surface and one that travels down through the film, reflects at the lower surface, and travels back up. The upper reflection is from lower index to higher index, so it gains a pi phase shift; the lower reflection is from higher index to lower index, so it gains no phase shift. The second ray also accumulates propagation phase for a round trip distance 2t in the film, equal to 4pi t/lambda. For constructive interference in reflected light, the net phase difference must be an integer multiple of 2pi, so 4pi t/lambda plus the single extra pi reversal condition gives the first constructive thickness t = lambda/4.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the film is the central layer labeled n_f, with light entering normally from the upper low-index medium and the lower medium also lower index than the film. From the text, lambda is the wavelength in the film. Instead of tracking absolute phases ray-by-ray, classify the thin-film case: because the film has higher refractive index than both adjacent materials, reflected light has exactly one phase inversion between the two relevant reflected rays. For reflected-light constructive interference with one phase inversion, the standard condition is that the round-trip optical path inside the film be a half-integer number of wavelengths: 2t = (m + 1/2)lambda. The minimum nonzero thickness is therefore t = lambda/4.
